rationale: Retain the original eight-hospital lessor partnership once under its legal entity Silver Holdco JV, LLC, preserve Medical Properties Partnership as an alias, record Macquarie/MIP V and Medical Properties Trust as former 50% owners, and mark the platform realized in 2024 after Steward's lease termination and the court-approved lender transition. Nonprofit operators, Massachusetts, Apollo's workout pool and property SPVs are successors or components rather than new manager-level PortCos.

evidence.purpose: Original platform identity, infrastructure mandate, ownership split and asset boundary.
supports: MIP V and Medical Properties Trust formed a 50/50 partnership for eight Massachusetts hospitals.
The original platform was a long-duration hospital real-estate lessor vehicle.
The transaction legally closed on March 14, 2022.
The original eight-property vehicle was approximately 55% financed with nonrecourse debt.
The Steward lease ended in 2024 and the collateral transitioned to Apollo-managed lenders.
Medical Properties Trust reserved its partnership equity and no active original platform remained.
Five sites had been sold, St. Elizabeth's was state-owned, and Carney and Nashoba remained in a lender workout vehicle at June 30, 2026.
No continuing Macquarie or Medical Properties Trust interest in the original partnership was identified.

companyFieldUpdates.name: Silver Holdco JV, LLC
aliases: MIP V / MPT Massachusetts hospital partnership
companyFieldUpdates.description: Silver Holdco JV, LLC was the 50/50 Macquarie Infrastructure Partners V and Medical Properties Trust lessor partnership for eight Steward-operated Massachusetts hospitals. The approximately US$1.7bn portfolio closed on March 14, 2022 under long-term triple-net leases. Steward's 2024 bankruptcy ended the lease economics, and Macquarie and Medical Properties Trust surrendered the collateral and cash to Apollo-managed lenders in exchange for debt releases. Five hospitals were subsequently sold, St. Elizabeth's transferred to Massachusetts, and Carney and Nashoba remained in a separate lender workout vehicle. The original Silver Holdco platform is therefore realized from 2024; successor operators, government transferees, individual property SPVs and the lender workout pool are not counted as successor PortCos.
